arjun: Heads up — I found a perf regression in serving where kernel selection flips around seq_len ~128 and we see ~+18% p95 latency for small prompts. Captured a short nsys run but the trace looked noisy and I think sampling window was too short.

maya: Can you share the exact nsys command you used?

arjun: Used a quick smoke capture to avoid huge files:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o tmp/kv-short -t 6s 
# (we did a single request-run inside the window)
```

kevin: Short captures are fine but they often miss the kernel switch if warmup + batch alignment doesn't fall inside the bracket. For this kind of kernel-selection hunt, I usually do bracketed capture with NVTX markers and a bit longer sampling window, e.g.:
```
# instrumented run (python):
# NVTX push before warmup loops, pop after steady-state
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o profs/kv-bracket --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=warmup_start --capture-range-end=steady_end --sample=cpu --duration=12s
```

maya: What values for sample window / duration do you recommend? I don't want 1GB traces but want the kernel switch visible.

arjun: In practice: do 2s warmup, 6–8s steady, 2s tail. So total ~12s. Set --sample=cpu (or --sample=none + rely on osrt for GPU scheduling events) and use --capture-range with NVTX to filter. Also add `--stop-after-target-exec` equivalent on our harness if possible.

perf-bot: Profile uploaded: https://internal-artifacts/profs/kv-bracket/4210001111 (12.3MB) :white_check_mark:

kevin: NVTX markers are key — wrap both the batching layer and the KV cache refill path. That way you can see: 1) kernel selection boundary, 2) whether KV eviction/prefetch overlaps the decision, 3) memcpy vs kernel overlap. If you see a kernel change at ~2.1s in the timeline that's the decision point.

arjun: From the quick flame/timeline I extracted a tiny snippet (simplified):
```
2.06s  cudaMemcpyAsync H2D  (prefetch)
2.09s  kernel: fused_attention_fwd (fast path)
2.12s  kernel: generic_attention_fwd (fallback)  <-- switch
2.13s  memcpy overlaps kernel (blocking)
```
That overlap looks like the scheduler picked a generic kernel because some prefetch landed late and forced a different workspace size.

maya: Good clue. I'll add NVTX bracketing around the prefetch + batcher and run the 12s capture. I'll post the timeline and a couple of screenshots.

arjun: Also try forcing the kernel selection env var on one run to confirm causality (set FAST_ATTEN=0/1 in harness) and compare traces. If the forced run keeps the fast kernel and latency improves, we've got the root cause.

kevin: One final tip — when capturing on multi-GPU test rigs, pin the process to a single GPU and disable background daemon timers (watchdog) to reduce osrt noise. Use `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` + `taskset` when possible.

maya: Will do. Thanks — I'll post results later today :thumbsup:
